content:
Maya: quick heads up — canary routing is sending ~4% of requests for the 'redwood-test' org to the projectless fallback bucket, which is blowing past the quota
Sam: saw the spike in quota alerts, wondered if it was a prometheus scrape fluke. thanks for calling it out
Jorge: are those requests coming with service-account tokens or plain api keys?
Maya: mostly api keys according to initial sampling. token claims show project_id=null even when tenant header present
Nikki: hmm. that suggests the claim extraction path is losing the header claim before routing decision. could be a middleware ordering issue
Erin: can you paste an example request/trace?
Maya: here's a trimmed trace from the canary router:
```
curl -X POST https://infer.redwood/api/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_abc123" 
  -H "X-Project-ID: proj-42" 
  -H "X-Origin-Org: redwood-test" 
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
router log:
```
[6801234567.001] TRACE router: recv req id=tx-9a8b 
[6801234567.002] TRACE auth: introspect token => claims:{iss:api-key, project_id:null, org_id:"redwood-test"} 
[6801234567.003] DECISION router: project_claim absent -> check header X-Project-ID (found: proj-42) -> but header_checker returned null due to header-mapping middleware ordering
[6801234567.004] FALLBACK router: route -> projectless-bucket(org-redwood-test)
```
Sam: so header mapping is running after the routing decision. that would do it
Jorge: we recently moved header normalization into a separate filter to centralize. maybe the filter isn't shimming claims for routing cache keys
Nikki: confirmed — middleware order changed in rollout #4512. the header->claim shim now runs after rate-limit lookup to avoid cache key explosion. that was intentional but seems to break project routing for api-keys
Erin: options:
- re-order shim before rate-limit lookup (fast, risk increasing cache cardinality)
- teach router to consult raw headers as fallback before rate-limit hit (more invasive)
Tony: we should prefer correctness for canary. revert ordering for the shim but add a cardinality guard: only copy X-Project-ID into claim when present and matches project allowlist
Maya: agree. we can do a targeted revert for canary and push a guard on the shim to prevent wildcarding many different header values
Nikki: I'll prepare a patch. small change to middleware chain + a config flag `shim.allowlist_projects`
Erin: I'll add a dashboard tile: projectless-routes %, per-org, and a telemetry alert if >1% sustained
Sam: also add a telemetry trace link from the dashboard to the raw router trace so engs can jump into examples
Tony: can we canary the shim-reorder to 10% first?
Maya: yes, 10% canary. if metrics look good escalate to 50% then full rollout. update runbook to note the quota impact and rollback path
deploy-bot: deploy request created: PR #5872 -> staging-canary (10%). CI tests pass. :rocket:
Jorge: pinging infra to make sure rate-limit cache behavior is acceptable for 10%
Nikki: PR up, includes guard and config toggle. link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/5872
Maya: thanks — will watch the dashboard over next 30m. if we still see projectless drop after reorder, we dig deeper into token introspector
Sam: :thumbsup: good plan
Erin: dashboard tile and alert created: https://dashboards/redwood/c/projectless-routes
Tony: I'll schedule a quick post-mortem doc if canary shows weirdness
Maya: closing loop: once canary OK, we schedule full rollout and add QA test covering header->claim mapping for api-keys
Sam: noted. thanks everyone
